newsitem.title: USA: Mark IV to sell audio unit to Greenwich St Capital.
newsitem.headline: Mark IV to sell audio unit to Greenwich St Capital.

text.p: Mark IV Industries, Inc. Thursday said it has agreed to sell its professional audio business, Mark IV Audio, to an affiliate of Greenwich Street Capital Partners, Inc. for $151.5 million in cash.
Greenwich Street Capital, a New York-based private equity fund, is expected to rename the business, which manufactures professional audio products, EV International, Inc.

Mark IV Audio is one of several non-core businesses being sold as part of Mark IV's effort to focus on its core power transmission, fluid transfer and filtration technologies businesses that serve global industrial and automotive markets.
Mark IV Audio had revenue of $195.5 million in the fiscal year ended Feb. 29, 1996.
The deal will result in a gain during the fourth quarter. Cash proceeds will initially be used to pay down bank debt, said the Amherst, N.Y.-based company.
The deal brings to about $254 million in proceeds from Mark IV's asset sales so far this fiscal year.

"Over the longer term, the capital capacity created by the divestiture programme may be used to make acquisitions in our core businesses, and/or to repurchase the company's common stock." said Sal Alfiero, Mark IV's chairman and chief executive.
The deal is expected to close in the fiscal fourth quarter, subject to regulatory approvals.
Mark IV has about 17,600 employees worldwide. The company's stock rose 37.5 cents to $21.50 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
